device.name: LEDs2RAVE4 / Lunchbox Dream LED (SP107E/SP110E/SPOTLED)
device.notes:
SPI LED pixel controllers and matrix panels used in LEDs2RAVE4 / Lunchbox Dream LED products. The generations do not share one protocol:
  * SP107E ("LED Chord") — Nordic UART service 0xFFE0, single characteristic
    0xFFE1 (write + notify). Fixed 4-byte command frame [d0, d1, d2, cmd_byte];
    no length prefix or checksum. check_device (cmd 0x01) returns 15 bytes.
  * SP110E ("LED Hue") — the same 0xFFE0/0xFFE1 channel but a different
    4-byte opcode set (the sp110e_* commands below).
  * SPOTLED matrix panels (com.led.spotled) — service 0xFF20, FF21 command
    and FF22 data. Data payloads use a 15-byte header (uint32 header length
    15, uint16 command type 0x8004, uint32 serial, uint32 content length,
    1-byte checksum), followed by typed records. The complete record and
    effect tables are in spotled-led-panel.yaml, the canonical reference.
  * Recent iLEDColor DreamPanel v3 boards — separate A950/A951/A952/A953
    protocol in iledcolor-led-panel.yaml. A tested unit had no FF20 service;
    iLEDColor is not a cloud-only or unmapped target.

DESIGN APP PER GENERATION (the app, not the model name, identifies the protocol):
  * Dream LED Skin v1        -> LED CHORD (com.spled.pzse)   -> SP107E, 0xFFE0
  * Dream LED Skin 2.0       -> SPOTLED   (com.led.spotled)  -> framed, 0xFF20
  * Dream Skin 3.0 early     -> SPOTLED   (com.led.spotled)  -> framed, 0xFF20
  * Dream Skin 3.0 recent    -> iLEDColor (com.led.iledcolor) -> A950
LEDs2RAVE4 changed the DreamPanel v3 controller board mid-production-run. If the panel's serial number renders horizontally, the unit needs iLEDColor; vertical selects SPOTLED.
SPOTLED upload flow is device-driven: write (MTU - 3) byte chunks and, when ContinueSending (type 255) arrives, resume from its offset rather than your own cursor. Do not wait at a fixed buffer_size/chunk_size threshold: the vendor sender paces writes and reacts to device responses. SendingDataFinish succeeds with response type 4, status 0, not type 2. PauseSending (type 254) can indicate bad MTU, but was also observed rejecting an eight-frame RGB payload; it is not proof of an MTU problem. GetDisplayInfo returns real width, height, colour depth (16 mono / 255 RGB), advertised frame limit, brightness and font info — query it instead of hardcoding a panel size. The tested unit reported 96x16 RGB, frame limit 20 and a 7280-byte buffer.
CONFIDENCE: the SPOTLED UUIDs, queries, static RGB upload and single-frame native scroll are hardware-confirmed. Multi-frame RGB limits, AE30/FF10 roles and the SP107E/SP110E live command tables remain open. SP107E static colour is 0x0C, not 0x04 (RGB order); SP110E speed is 0x00-0xFF. The full SP107E opcode map and 26-byte status layout are documented in UniLED. SPOTLED is deprecated on recent Android; LEDs2RAVE4 recommends a sideload or PIXELY GLOW. The LED Chord / LED Hue seller is Shenzhen Sperll Optoelectronic Technology Co., Ltd.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write. Verification covers the SPOTLED generation; SP107E/SP110E remain source-derived.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect, enable FF21 notifications on SPOTLED, then query BufferSize and DisplayInfo before uploading.

setup.notes: No provisioning. SP107E/SP110E controllers accept a connection from any central; the LED strip layout is configured by command after connecting, not during setup. The SPOTLED query and upload onboarding path was exercised successfully on 2026-11-07.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

testing.notes: On 2026-11-07 this project queried one SPOTLED unit (96x16 RGB, 7280-byte receive buffer), uploaded a static RGB frame and completed a single-frame native scroll-left upload with success acknowledgements. An eight-frame full-RGB upload was rejected with response 254, so arbitrary multi-frame support is not claimed. SP107E, SP110E and other panel geometries remain untested; iLEDColor hardware is covered by its own spec.

entities.name: LED Strip
entities.notes: SP110E dialect of the same 0xFFE1 channel — the two variants share the characteristic but not the opcode set, hence the per-variant entities. All sp110e_* opcodes are secondary-source; verify on hardware.

features.notes: A 96x16 RGB static upload and a single-frame native scroll-left upload completed at MTU 512 in ten chunks with type-2 start and type-4 finish success responses. GetDisplayInfo supplies geometry. An eight-frame full-RGB upload was rejected with response 254, so the advertised 20-frame field is not treated as a proven multi-frame limit.

remaining_unknowns: SP107E and SP110E commands remain source-derived; no live capture verifies their characteristic properties or per-variant tables.

The tested SPOTLED unit rejected an eight-frame full-RGB payload with response 254. Its true multi-frame/resource limit and the meaning of the advertised frame-limit field need an official-app capture.
AE30 and FF10 were enumerated on the SPOTLED unit but not used; their roles are unknown.
Static RGB and single-frame native scrolling are confirmed only on the tested 96x16 unit. Other geometries, text/font records, brightness/screen-mode writes and factory reset remain unverified.
iLEDColor settings beyond the separate spec's confirmed Connect/TestPass and upload flows remain open.

sp107e_set_color.description: SP107E: Set static RGB colour (cmd 0x0C — NOT 0x04; 0x04 is SET_RGB_SEQ colour order and would reprogram the chip's RGB sequence)

sp107e_set_effect.description: SP107E: Set effect 0x01-0xB4 dynamic, 0xB5 static (secondary source, verify)

sp107e_status_query.description: SP107E: Query status, returns 26 bytes in 2 packets (secondary source, verify)

sp110e_set_color.description: SP110E: Set static RGB colour (secondary source, verify)

sp110e_set_effect.description: SP110E: Set effect 0x01-0x78 dynamic, 0x79 static (secondary source, verify)

sp110e_set_speed.description: SP110E: Set animation speed 0x00-0xFF (secondary source, verify)

sp110e_status_query.description: SP110E: Query device status, returns 12 bytes (secondary source, verify)

characteristics.name: Control
characteristics.notes: Fixed 4-byte command frame [d0, d1, d2, cmd_byte]; no length prefix, no checksum. Notifications (e.g. check_device's 15-byte reply) arrive on this same characteristic. Confidence: core opcodes HIGH, others MEDIUM. SP110E hardware uses this same service/characteristic with its own 4-byte opcode set (mbullington sp110e.md gist: "My device's service id is 0xFFE0 and has one characteristic 0xFFE1") — the sp110e_* commands below. The full SP107E opcode map and 26-byte status layout are decoded in monty68/uniled led_chord.py.

spotled_get_buffer_size.description: SPOTLED: device data buffer size (7-byte content after the two-byte response header).

spotled_get_display_info.description: SPOTLED: query big-endian width, height, colour depth (16 mono / 255 RGB), advertised frame limit, brightness and font info (11-byte content after the two-byte response header).

spotled_get_version.description: SPOTLED: device type + device/software revision (13-byte content after the two-byte response header).

spotled_sending_data_finish.description: SPOTLED: payload fully transmitted. Expect response type 4 with matching serial/type and status zero, not type 2.

spotled_sending_data_start.description: SPOTLED: announce an incoming data payload. Expect response type 2 with matching serial/type and status zero.

characteristics.name: Command
characteristics.notes: SPOTLED app protocol (com.led.spotled), live-confirmed on a 96x16 RGB unit. Canonical reference: spotled-led-panel.yaml — keep in sync. Commands are complete frames and must not receive another framing layer. Notification values have a two-byte outer header [total_length][response_type], followed by the documented content. SendingDataFinish succeeds with response type 4 and status zero.

characteristics.name: Data
characteristics.notes: Bulk data channel (used alongside FF21). Payload structure and typed records are canonical in spotled-led-panel.yaml. Write (MTU - 3) byte chunks and react to device-driven ContinueSending (type 255) offsets; do not assume a fixed buffer-full threshold. PauseSending (type 254) may mean bad MTU but also rejected an eight-frame RGB payload, whose exact limiting factor remains unresolved.

initialization.notes: Await the type-21 BufferSize notification, not an ATT read.
